key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: RAPID onset within minutes of exposure to allergen. LOCATION: Systemic, affecting multiple organ systems. DURATION: Minutes to hours, can be life-threatening. CHARACTER: Severe, rapidly progressive. AGGRAVATING: Continued allergen exposure. RELIEVING: Epinephrine, antihistamines, steroids. TIMING: Acute, rapid progression. SEVERITY: Severe to life-threatening (8-10/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Respiratory: stridor, wheezing, dyspnea, throat tightness. Cutaneous: urticaria, angioedema, pruritus. Cardiovascular: hypotension, tachycardia, shock. GI: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. Neurological: altered mental status, dizziness. KEY POSITIVES: Multi-system involvement, rapid onset, known allergen exposure. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no chest pain (unless secondary to respiratory distress).
